title: nexus.mcp.client
description: MCP client bridge. Every key here is read by parseConfig/parseServer/parseToolFilter/applyResourceConfig in plugins/mcp/client/config.go — the schema is derived from those readers, so an unknown key is a key the plugin would have silently ignored. Duplicate names across servers[] are rejected by parseConfig after the loop; JSON Schema cannot express that cross-item constraint, so it stays a runtime check.

aliases.description: Short slash command -> "<server>.<prompt>". With the default command_prefix, `review: gh.review_pr` makes /review rewrite to /mcp.gh.review_pr. Values must be strings: parseConfig drops any entry whose value is not a non-empty string.

servers.description: One entry per MCP server. Absent or empty means the plugin connects nothing.

defaults.description: Inherited by every servers[] entry unless overridden inline. Note there is no `tools` key here — tool filters are per-server only.

lifecycle.description: Default connect/disconnect timing for every server. Default "engine".

timeout.description: Default per-RPC timeout for tools/call, resources/read, prompts/get. Default 30s.

command_prefix.description: First segment of the slash command registered per MCP prompt. Default "mcp", so server `fake` prompt `greet` becomes /mcp.fake.greet.

server.description: One MCP server connection. The key set is flat and identical for every transport — parseServer reads command, url and server unconditionally — but which of them is REQUIRED depends on transport. That per-transport requirement is expressed by the allOf/if/then branches below so a missing key fails at boot naming the key, instead of surfacing from parseServer during the connect phase.

name.description: Required. Namespaces every catalog entry (mcp__<name>__<tool>) and slash command. Same pattern parseServer enforces. Must be unique across servers[] — that check is a runtime one.

transport.description: How the connection is made. "stdio" launches `command` as a subprocess, "http" dials `url` over the streamable HTTP transport, "inprocess" wires an in-memory transport to the *mcp.Server the host registered under `server` via RegisterInProcessServer before engine.Boot(). Defaults to "stdio" when absent.

command.description: Required for transport: stdio. Executable to launch, resolved on PATH. No ~ expansion — write an absolute path.

args.description: Argument list passed to `command`. Strings only: parseServer skips non-string elements.

env.description: Environment exported to the stdio subprocess. ${VAR} references expand from the host environment at parse time (unset expands to empty), so the expansion is invisible to this schema and values are typed as plain strings.

env_passthrough.description: Names of host environment variables forwarded verbatim to the subprocess. Silently skipped when unset on the host.

url.description: Required for transport: http. Base URL of the streamable HTTP MCP endpoint.

headers.description: HTTP headers attached to every request. ${VAR} references expand from the host environment (see `env`).

server.description: Required for transport: inprocess. The opaque key a host passed to client.RegisterInProcessServer(key, *mcp.Server) BEFORE engine.Boot(). The registry is process-wide, so a multi-engine host must scope keys per agent/tenant.

allOf.description: stdio requires command. The `if` deliberately does NOT require `transport`: an absent transport defaults to stdio in parseServer, and an absent property matches vacuously, so both spellings land here.
http requires url. `required: [transport]` in the `if` stops an absent transport from matching vacuously — without it, a stdio server would be asked for a url.
inprocess requires server (see the http branch for why `required: [transport]` is there).

tools.description: Per-server allowlist/blocklist, matched against the RAW MCP tool name, not the mcp__<server>__<tool> catalog name. Deny wins over allow; an empty allow list means everything is allowed.

allow.description: When non-empty, only these raw tool names reach the catalog.

resources.description: How MCP resources are surfaced. Identical key set under `defaults` and under a servers[] entry — applyResourceConfig parses both, layering the server block over the inherited defaults.

enabled.description: Toggle the whole resource surface. Default true.

auto_register_static.description: Register every static resource as a no-arg catalog tool. Default true.

auto_register_template.description: Register every resource template as a catalog tool whose inputSchema mirrors the template variables. Default true.

auto_register_max.description: Static auto-registration is skipped when the server returns more static resources than this, leaving only the generic list_resources/read_resource tools. Default 50. An integer here (unlike `timeout`, which is string-only): applyResourceConfig reads it through intLike, which accepts int, int64 and float64. A negative value is silently ignored by that reader, so it is rejected here instead.

subscribe_updates.description: Subscribe to resources/updated for each auto-registered static resource; notifications produce mcp.resource.updated events. Default true.

prompts.description: The prompt slash-command surface. `enabled` is its only key, under both `defaults` and a servers[] entry.

enabled.description: Toggle prompt slash commands for the server. Default true.

lifecycle.description: When servers connect and disconnect. "engine" = on engine boot/shutdown. "session" = on io.session.start / io.session.end.

duration.description: A Go duration string such as "30s", "10m" or "1h30m". A bare number is rejected on purpose: parseServer reads timeout only through a `string` type assertion, so a YAML number is silently ignored and the default is used instead — exactly the kind of quiet miss this schema exists to stop.
